text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'spot-eu-west-2a' saturation (queue > 1200). autoscaler failing to allocate; 95% GPU utilization; preemptible eviction spike detected. Paging oncall.

ashok: ack — I'm on call. seeing the same in the console. Autoscaler logs show repeated 503 from cloud API when requesting new VMs. Queue growth started ~13:02 UTC, current tail latency > 6s for generation endpoints.

maria: adding context — preemptible eviction wave at 12:58 UTC in the region. Fallback capacity pool (dedicated-burst) shows 0 available nodes, reserved quota fully used by long-running jobs.

tim: dug into runtime logs. KV cache thrash happened after several prefixes were evicted; that plus continuous batching backlog is making per-request latency spike and tokens/timeouts. Also seeing many 'scale request denied: quota limit' errors from autoscaler:
```
E0313 13:05:12 autoscaler.go:412] scale request failed: RequestError: Request limit exceeded
caused by: QuotaExceeded: Could not allocate CPUs in eu-west-2a
```

beth: support report — starting to get customer tickets for timeouts and partial responses. Most are from a single enterprise on a high-throughput route. Triage: about 18 unique customers affected, ~1.1% of total traffic in the window.

lia: product impact note — the slowdown affects both chat and generation; embeddings are mostly fine (different pool). We should flag impacted customers and suggest mitigation.

ashok: immediate mitigation plan: 1) open provider ticket for quota/eviction explanation, 2) temporarily relax per-request concurrency limits for premium customers on dedicated pool (if we can free capacity), 3) enable fallback to on-demand nodes for core routes, 4) scale down long-running low-priority jobs. I'm going to attempt (4) now.

kevin: I'm on infra, will attempt to suspend non-critical reserved jobs and spin up 2 on-demand p3d nodes as temp capacity. ETA ~8 minutes if cloud API responds.

ashok: while kevin works that, we should also reduce batching windows to process queue faster. tim, can we lower the batch_window_ms and force immediate batch flush for the critical model routes?

tim: yes. pushing a hot config change to runtime batcher now:
```bash
# change batch window to 5ms for route /v1/generate-critical
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" \"$RUNTIME_API/configs/batcher\" -d '{"routes": {"/v1/generate-critical": {"batch_window_ms": 5}}}'
```
apply in 30s. watch logs for backlog drain.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-batcher-config-update started by tim.

maria: small note — prefix caching is still being invalidated because KV store eviction due to memory pressure on a subset of nodes. If we free up 2 nodes, we should prefer bringing back nodes with largest cache residency.

ashok: good point. kevin, when spinning up on-demand, label them with cache-priority: high to ensure routing.

kevin: done. requested 2 on-demand nodes with label cache-priority=high. Cloud API accepted requests at 13:12 UTC, but provisioning stalled at 13:14 with a transient 429 from provider. retrying.

carlos: CS update: notified top impacted customers in bulk at 13:16 UTC — said we are investigating and will provide ETA. One customer is asking for a failover to their dedicated deployment; they have a Private plan but not currently deployed. Lia says we can offer temporary priority and credits.

beth: logged affected customer IDs (redwood-corp-5, bluechair, analytics-inc) in the incident ticket. escalation to account ops recommended for enterprise SLA checks.

ashok: current metrics at 13:18 UTC: queue size 1186 -> 940 after small config change; 5xx rate peaked at 1.8% and now ~0.9%. Tail latency 95p down from 6.2s to 3.8s. Progress but still not healthy.

maria: autoscaler logs show backoff loop triggered by quota errors. Suggest short-term workaround: switch autoscaler to 'prov-on-demand-override' mode to allow on-demand allocation when spot fails. We need approval from infra owners.

tim: downside — on-demand increases cost but avoids customer impact. If infra signs off, I can flip it. It has a guarded flag in the control plane.

kevin: infra approves temporary override for the incident window. I'll coordinate cost alerting so finance is aware.

ashok: grant approved. tim, flip the guard. Also please add a safety cap: only 20% of peak can be on-demand to limit cost.

tim: flipping override now.
```bash
POST $CONTROLPLANE/api/autoscaler/override 
{ "mode": "on-demand-allowed", "max_on_demand_pct": 20 }
```
apply at 13:22 UTC.

deploy-bot: autoscaler override applied by tim.

maria: we're seeing on-demand allocations succeed; 2 on-demand nodes up at 13:27 UTC. queue down to 400 and tail latency 95p ~1.6s. 5xx now ~0.3%.

beth: customers getting better responses. sent update at 13:29 UTC. tickets decreasing.

lia: product wants a short post-incident note for impacted customers describing root cause and remediation steps; also call out that on-demand was used as temporary fallback.

ashok: preliminary root cause: preemptible eviction storm reduced spot pool by ~64% leading to autoscaler quota/backoff interactions and inability to fallback because dedicated-burst pool had no spare nodes (occupied by long-running low-priority jobs). Combined with KV cache evictions and batching backlog, this created backpressure and throttling.

maria: suggested followups: 1) add guardrails to avoid long-running jobs occupying reserved burst capacity (runbook change), 2) make autoscaler more resilient to transient quota errors (retry/backoff jitter tuning), 3) add faster soft-fallback path to on-demand with cost controls, 4) improve cache eviction heuristics to preserve hot prefixes during transient node churn.

kevin: infra action items: temporarily reclaim reserved-burst capacity by preempting non-critical training jobs, schedule provider support call to understand eviction patterns, request increase in quota or reduce per-AZ affinity to spread risk.

carlos: CS to prepare customer-facing summary and offer credits to impacted customers. Will coordinate with finance and lia.

beth: documenting SLO impact: 13:02–13:28 UTC window, error budget consumption for generation tier was ~0.6%. Will add to incident ticket.

ashok: handing over to night oncall (kevin) at 13:40 UTC — we've stabilized with on-demand fallback but some followups are outstanding. kevin, please monitor queue, 5xx rate, and autoscaler backoff logs. I'll post runbook steps and assign followups.

kevin: ack. will monitor and escalate if things regress. leaving the autoscaler override in place until we validate quota/backfill with provider, scheduled check at 16:00 UTC.

tim: creating a short-term patch PR to add jitter and exponential backoff to autoscaler cloud requests, plus a feature flag to bypass certain quota errors after N retries. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/421

maria: raising a postmortem channel and placeholder doc. Please add timelines and metrics.

lia: thanks everyone. CS will send an update to affected customers by 14:00 UTC.

ashok: closing note — this incident shows two coupled failure modes: provider-side eviction storms and internal capacity/placement policies that allowed critical fallback pools to be fully consumed by low-priority workloads. We'll propose policy changes to prevent reserved pools from being saturated by low-priority workloads.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev2. Duration: 00:38:32. Primary owner: ashok.

kevin: handover complete at 13:40 UTC. leaving watch on until 16:00 UTC.

maria: will start postmortem draft after stabilization. Add any logs/screenshots you captured into the doc.

beth: final customer note queued for review.

(threads and followups will be tracked in the incident ticket #INC-2027)
